content:
Ava Li: Quick recap from today's runtime segment + a few follow-ups folks asked for. Dropping them here so it's searchable.
Markus Vogel: High-level: are we still splitting work into 'fast wins' (batching/caching) vs 'kernel refactor'? which gets headcount this quarter?
Ava Li: We committed 60/40 split in Q2: 60% of cycle for batching/caching/observability (low-hanging perf wins), 40% for kernel refactor work that unlocks quantized performance.
Rina Shah: For the batching effort, is the plan to change the default queueing heuristic? will routes see param changes?
Ava Li: Defaults remain conservative. New heuristic will be opt-in per-route via routing config: `batch_strategy: adaptive` with safe caps. We'll add templates for webhooks and low-latency routes.
Leo Kim: Any expected user-visible latency improvement numbers from adaptive batching? ballpark p95 drop?
Ava Li: Early sim shows ~15-22% p95 improvement on medium-traffic routes with 512 token avg. We'll publish benchmarks after canary.
Ethan Chen: Kernel team note: refactor focused on attention kernel tiling + reduced mem copies. That targets tail latencies and token-cost savings for q8/q4.
Janelle Torres: KV cache migration concerns: are we changing format? will older clients break?
Ethan Chen: No format break. Migration is internal: we add a compatibility header and a runtime shim for 6 weeks. Ops will open a migration-monitor dashboard.
Markus Vogel: Canary plan? percentages and rollback criteria so we can pre-create alerts.
Ava Li: Canary steps: 1) 2% -> 5% -> 20% over 48 hours if SLIs are green. Rollback triggers: p95 > 2x baseline, error rate increase > 0.5%, or eval-set accuracy drop > 4% on regen tests.
Rina Shah: Can we get the exact alert names so product owners can subscribe?
Ava Li: Will publish alert names in #eng-runtime. Draft: `runtime.canary.p95.spike`, `runtime.canary.error_rate`, `runtime.canary.eval_regress`.
ops-bot: Canary `kernel-tiling-v2` started: id c-20260401-01, 2% traffic. Monitoring enabled.
Leo Kim: If canary hits a false positive on eval_regress (no user visible issues), can we mark it a soft-fail?
Ethan Chen: We'll have a manual review step for eval anomalies under 5% traffic. If human review finds no degradation we'll proceed, but alerts still notify SRE/ML.
Janelle Torres: Docs/runbook ask: include clear steps to rollback a canary and to backfill model caches. Ops needs commands.
Ava Li: Agree. I'll coordinate with SRE to add runbook snippets and a `rails`-like playbook with commands and expected timings.
Markus Vogel: One more: caching TTLs — are we changing defaults? customers with streaming sessions saw stale prefix behavior last month.
Ava Li: Default prefix cache TTL stays short (30s) for streaming sessions. We will expose `prefix_cache_ttl_ms` per-route and a 'session-aware' caching mode to reduce staleness.
Rina Shah: Who to ping when a canary looks noisy but not breaking?
Ava Li: Ping @Ethan Chen and #eng-runtime, and tag `oncall-sre`. We'll add a small binding in Console to raise a review ticket.
Ethan Chen: I'll post the canary results + perf graphs back into this thread when we have 20% traffic steady-state. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
